input: Please provide details of your main extracurricular interests and achievements. How have these interests and achievements helped you to develop the skills that you will need as a commercial solicitor? (350 words)
output:
Competitive team sport has shaped most of my life. I began at a local rugby club aged five and progressed to representing the x university 1st XV. Rugby’s intensity showed me that results depend on relationships built off the pitch as much as performance on it. Those interpersonal habits have carried into every workplace I have joined.

In Madrid, during my first week, I arranged coffee with two associates in the aviation team. Early rapport created a support network and made it easier to communicate honestly about my capacity. I see those same skills as essential for commercial solicitors, who must work effectively in teams and form durable relationships with colleagues and clients.

A concrete achievement was drafting x firm’s newsletter on EU drone regulations while based in the Madrid office. I had no prior knowledge of drones, so I researched across legal sources, translated findings into English, and drafted the piece while incorporating comments from London colleagues on a shared document. The unfamiliar subject matter and multi-step process were demanding, but supervisor praise on completion was rewarding. The task also pushed me to use Spanish in a business setting.

I balanced that drafting against legal translation work and a university Spanish course introduced because of the pandemic. Meeting those concurrent demands required disciplined time management—an electronic calendar, strict deadlines, and often late evenings—demonstrating resilience suited to pressured commercial practice.
